55	UI text is direct and never overclaims (the [feedback changelog](mockups/FEEDBACK-CHANGELOG.md) is a good model: "this is a prototype," "open for discussion"). The mischief lives in small, optional places — the smileybones, a dry empty state — never in anything load-bearing or anything a stressed researcher has to parse.
56	
57	### 7. Built to last by a small team
58	arXiv is daily infrastructure maintained by a very small team. Designs must be **low-maintenance**: no patterns that require manual upkeep, no per-paper hand-tuning, citation formats generated from metadata ([DESIGN-POLICIES](DESIGN-POLICIES.md)). Durable and boring-where-it-counts beats clever-and-fragile. This too is "zero ego."
59	
60	### 8. Speed and efficiency are different promises
61	For arXiv these are two distinct pillars, not synonyms. **Speed** is how fast a paper moves from submission to published and announced: a throughput commitment. **Efficiency** is how few clicks it takes a researcher to get what they came for, whether that's the DOI, the PDF, the source, or the right version. Publisher sites bury those behind many clicks; arXiv surfaces them. The design directive that follows: count the clicks to every core task (download, cite, find the DOI, switch version) and minimize them. The common cases belong on the surface, not in menus.

UI text is direct and never overclaims (the [feedback changelog](mockups/FEEDBACK-CHANGELOG.md) is a good model: "this is a prototype," "open for discussion"). The mischief lives in small, optional places — the smileybones, a dry empty state — never in anything load-bearing or anything a stressed researcher has to parse.

arXiv is daily infrastructure maintained by a very small team. 7	
8	## The arXiv palette
9	
10	### Primary colors — browns & blues
11	
12	These are arXiv's core identity colors post-spinout. They carry the weight of the brand on both internal and public platforms.
13	
14	| Name | Hex | Role |
15	|---|---|---|
16	| **Repository Brown** | `#1c1a17` | Body text, dark backgrounds, primary headers |
17	| **Library Grey** | `#6b6459` | Secondary text, labels, muted interactive elements (5.83:1 on white) |
18	| **UI Boundary Grey** | `#8b8680` | Interactive borders, tracks, arrows — WCAG 3:1 compliant (3.61:1 on white) |
19	| **Disabled Grey** | `#b0aba6` | Disabled states, exempt from WCAG contrast requirements |
20	| **Link Blue** | `#1565c0` | All interactive links, light mode (5.74:1 on white) |
21	| **Link Hover** | `#1050a0` | Link hover state (7.83:1 on white) |
22	| **Visited Purple** | `#7b2fbe` | Visited link state (7.02:1 on white) |
23	| **Archival Blue** | `#1f5e96` | Brand accent blue. Candidate for public button identity. Close to Link Blue — may need to shift for differentiation. |
24	| **Open Blue** | `#a5d6fe` | Public primary action fill (with Repository Brown text, 11.3:1 AA); also a light-blue tint for section backgrounds and highlights |
25	
26	### Accent colors
27	
28	Used for energy and personality. These are "pop" colors, not workhorses.
29	
30	| Name | Hex | Contrast on white | Suitable for |
31	|---|---|---|---|
32	| **Access Lime** | `#c4d82e` | ~1.5:1 | Background fills, badges, accent stripes. NOT for text or small elements. |
33	| **Smileybones Yellow** | `#ffe000` | ~1.3:1 | Background fills, the smileybones icon, celebratory/playful accents. NOT for text or fine detail. |
34	
35	Both accent colors fail text contrast on white — they are strictly "big gesture" colors for fills, borders at sufficient thickness, and graphic elements.
36	
37	If a darker yellow is needed for smaller accents (thin borders, small badges), a golden variant like `#d4b800` (~2.5:1 on white) could work while staying in the yellow family. This would need to be derived from the original if the use case arises.
38	
39	### Heritage colors — used sparingly
40	
41	These connect arXiv to its history. They are not primary brand colors post-spinout.
42	
43	| Name | Hex | Origin | Usage |
44	|---|---|---|---|
45	| **Campus Red** | `#b31b1b` | Formerly "Cornell Red" | The X in the arXiv logo. Very occasional accent — a thin rule, a hover detail. Never for headers, buttons, large color fields, or text. |
46	| **Publishing Pink** | `#fb595a` | Complement to Campus Red | Rare accent for playful or celebratory contexts. Announcements, limited-time callouts. Never for errors or body text. |
47	
48	### Functional colors — shared
49	
50	These serve specific UI functions and are not part of the brand identity.
51	
52	| Name | Hex | Role |
53	|---|---|---|
54	| **Danger Red** | `#c62828` | Destructive actions, error states. Distinct from Campus Red — this is functional, not brand. |
55	| **Focus Ring** | `#1565c0` light / `#64b5f6` dark | Keyboard focus indicator |
56	
57	### Status & alert colors — shared
58	
59	Semantic colors for the `.ds-alert` component and any success / informational / warning / error messaging. One system on both public (white) and internal (Warm Wash) surfaces, light and dark. Each state is also distinguished by an icon and a leading word — never color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). All text/background pairings clear AA; most clear AAA.
60	
61	| State | Light bg | Light border | Light text/icon | Dark bg | Dark border | Dark text/icon | Text contrast (light / dark) |
62	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
63	| **Success** | `#e8f5d8` | `#6b8e1e` | `#4a5a0a` | `#1e2b0d` | `#8fbd3a` | `#c5e1a5` | 6.7:1 / 10.4:1 |
64	| **Info** | `#e7f1fd` | `#5a82c8` | `#1a3a78` | `#132433` | `#64b5f6` | `#90caf9` | 9.6:1 / 9.0:1 |
65	| **Warning** | `#fff8e1` | `#e8b800` | `#7a5c00` | `#2e2410` | `#e8b800` | `#ffe082` | 5.9:1 / 11.8:1 |
66	| **Error / failure** | `#fdeaea` | `#c62828` | `#8b0000` | `#2d1414` | `#e57373` | `#ef9a9a` | 8.6:1 / 8.0:1 |
67	
68	Why these values:
69	
70	- **Success is lime-olive, not forest green.** arXiv has no success-green, and Access Lime `#c4d82e` is reserved as the "staff tools" signal *and* fails text contrast — so it can't double as success. Rather than introduce a new green family, success reuses the existing `.seg-positive` lime-olive (bg `#e8f5d8`, text `#4a5a0a`) with the border pulled off-yellow (`#6b8e1e` — lower red channel than `--sec-border` `#9cb522`) so it reads as "success," not "brand accent." A forest-green alternative was considered and rejected to keep the palette tight.
71	- **Info is navy, deliberately darker than Link Blue** `#1565c0`, so an info banner is never mistaken for a link. Reuses the `.seg-neutral` / `.type-new` family.
72	- **Warning is the existing version-warning amber** (`#fff8e1` / `#e8b800` / `#7a5c00`), promoted from the one-off abstract-page banner.
73	- **Error reuses Danger Red** `#c62828` for the border, with a light tint background and the `.seg-negative` deep-red text `#8b0000`.
74	
75	Tokens: internal `design-system.css` exposes `--success-*` / `--info-*` / `--warning-*` / `--error-*` (matching the unprefixed `--danger`); public `design-system.css` exposes the `--arxiv-`-prefixed equivalents. 88	| **Blue tint** | `#f0f5ff` | Code/identifier backgrounds, citation display boxes |

**Status:** Active
**Last updated:** 2026-07-24

## The arXiv palette

### Primary colors — browns & blues

These are arXiv's core identity colors post-spinout. They carry the weight of the brand on both internal and public platforms.

| Name | Hex | Role |
|---|---|---|
| **Repository Brown** | `#1c1a17` | Body text, dark backgrounds, primary headers |
| **Library Grey** | `#6b6459` | Secondary text, labels, muted interactive elements (5.83:1 on white) |
| **UI Boundary Grey** | `#8b8680` | Interactive borders, tracks, arrows — WCAG 3:1 compliant (3.61:1 on white) |
| **Disabled Grey** | `#b0aba6` | Disabled states, exempt from WCAG contrast requirements |
| **Link Blue** | `#1565c0` | All interactive links, light mode (5.74:1 on white) |
| **Link Hover** | `#1050a0` | Link hover state (7.83:1 on white) |
| **Visited Purple** | `#7b2fbe` | Visited link state (7.02:1 on white) |
| **Archival Blue** | `#1f5e96` | Brand accent blue. Candidate for public button identity. Close to Link Blue — may need to shift for differentiation. |
| **Open Blue** | `#a5d6fe` | Public primary action fill (with Repository Brown text, 11.3:1 AA); also a light-blue tint for section backgrounds and highlights |

### Accent colors

Used for energy and personality. These are "pop" colors, not workhorses.

| Name | Hex | Contrast on white | Suitable for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Access Lime** | `#c4d82e` | ~1.5:1 | Background fills, badges, accent stripes. NOT for text or small elements. |
| **Smileybones Yellow** | `#ffe000` | ~1.3:1 | Background fills, the smileybones icon, celebratory/playful accents. NOT for text or fine detail. |

Both accent colors fail text contrast on white — they are strictly "big gesture" colors for fills, borders at sufficient thickness, and graphic elements.

If a darker yellow is needed for smaller accents (thin borders, small badges), a golden variant like `#d4b800` (~2.5:1 on white) could work while staying in the yellow family. This would need to be derived from the original if the use case arises.

### Heritage colors — used sparingly

These connect arXiv to its history. They are not primary brand colors post-spinout.

| Name | Hex | Origin | Usage |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Campus Red** | `#b31b1b` | Formerly "Cornell Red" | The X in the arXiv logo. Very occasional accent — a thin rule, a hover detail. Never for headers, buttons, large color fields, or text. |
| **Publishing Pink** | `#fb595a` | Complement to Campus Red | Rare accent for playful or celebratory contexts. Announcements, limited-time callouts. Never for errors or body text. |

These serve specific UI functions and are not part of the brand identity.

| Name | Hex | Role |

| **Danger Red** | `#c62828` | Destructive actions, error states. Distinct from Campus Red — this is functional, not brand. |

### Status & alert colors — shared

Semantic colors for the `.ds-alert` component and any success / informational / warning / error messaging. One system on both public (white) and internal (Warm Wash) surfaces, light and dark. Each state is also distinguished by an icon and a leading word — never color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). All text/background pairings clear AA; most clear AAA.

| State | Light bg | Light border | Light text/icon | Dark bg | Dark border | Dark text/icon | Text contrast (light / dark) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Success** | `#e8f5d8` | `#6b8e1e` | `#4a5a0a` | `#1e2b0d` | `#8fbd3a` | `#c5e1a5` | 6.7:1 / 10.4:1 |
| **Info** | `#e7f1fd` | `#5a82c8` | `#1a3a78` | `#132433` | `#64b5f6` | `#90caf9` | 9.6:1 / 9.0:1 |
| **Warning** | `#fff8e1` | `#e8b800` | `#7a5c00` | `#2e2410` | `#e8b800` | `#ffe082` | 5.9:1 / 11.8:1 |
| **Error / failure** | `#fdeaea` | `#c62828` | `#8b0000` | `#2d1414` | `#e57373` | `#ef9a9a` | 8.6:1 / 8.0:1 |

Why these values:

- **Success is lime-olive, not forest green.** arXiv has no success-green, and Access Lime `#c4d82e` is reserved as the "staff tools" signal *and* fails text contrast — so it can't double as success. Rather than introduce a new green family, success reuses the existing `.seg-positive` lime-olive (bg `#e8f5d8`, text `#4a5a0a`) with the border pulled off-yellow (`#6b8e1e` — lower red channel than `--sec-border` `#9cb522`) so it reads as "success," not "brand accent." A forest-green alternative was considered and rejected to keep the palette tight.
- **Info is navy, deliberately darker than Link Blue** `#1565c0`, so an info banner is never mistaken for a link. Reuses the `.seg-neutral` / `.type-new` family.
- **Warning is the existing version-warning amber** (`#fff8e1` / `#e8b800` / `#7a5c00`), promoted from the one-off abstract-page banner.
- **Error reuses Danger Red** `#c62828` for the border, with a light tint background and the `.seg-negative` deep-red text `#8b0000`.

Tokens: internal `design-system.css` exposes `--success-*` / `--info-*` / `--warning-*` / `--error-*` (matching the unprefixed `--danger`); public `design-system.css` exposes the `--arxiv-`-prefixed equivalents. 1	# Typography Specification
2	
3	**Status:** Draft
4	**Scope:** All arXiv platforms — public-facing pages, internal tools, and HTML paper rendering
5	**Last updated:** 2026-06-17

9	## Font families
10	
11	arXiv uses the IBM Plex type family for all text, and STIX Two Math for mathematical notation. All fonts are self-hosted — no external font services (Google Fonts, Adobe Typekit, etc.).
12	
13	### Why IBM Plex
14	
15	- **Open source** — SIL Open Font License. No licensing cost, no vendor dependency.
16	- **Self-hostable** — woff2 files served from arXiv's own static assets. No external requests.
17	- **Complete family** — Sans, Sans Condensed, Mono, and Serif variants cover all use cases without mixing font families from different designers.
18	- **Language coverage** — supports Latin Extended, Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari, Thai, and more. Critical for an international research platform.
19	- **Math compatibility** — pairs well with STIX Two Math. Both are designed for technical/scientific contexts.
20	
21	### Why not other fonts
22	
23	- **Freight Sans/Text** (current brand font) — commercial, licensed through Cornell's Adobe Typekit account. Access will be lost with the Cornell spinout. Not self-hostable without a separate license purchase.
24	- **Rival Sans** (current HTML paper font) — commercial, also via Cornell's Typekit. Same dependency issue.
25	- **Google-hosted fonts** — internal objections to external font service dependencies. Self-hosting eliminates third-party requests, improves privacy, and ensures availability.
26	
27	---
28	
29	## Typeface re-evaluation — June 2026
30	
31	**Decision: stay with IBM Plex Sans.** A deep review (cited below) scored Plex against the strongest open-source alternatives — Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, Source Sans 3, Inter, Public Sans. Plex is the *only* open-source family that bundles a competent text face, broad Latin + Greek + Cyrillic coverage, OFL self-hosting, **and** a true Condensed cut, in one coherent family. No alternative ships a real condensed/narrow width, so switching wholesale would forfeit the dense-table capability arXiv depends on — the same completeness that drove the original choice.
32	
33	### Scored comparison
34	
35	| Criterion | **IBM Plex Sans** | Atkinson Hyperlegible Next | Source Sans 3 | Inter | Public Sans |
36	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
37	| Evidence-based readability | ✓ competent | ~ design-intent, unproven | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
38	| OFL + self-host (woff2) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
39	| Global names (Latin+Greek+Cyrillic) | ✓ core | ~ Latin diacritics; Greek/Cyrillic unconfirmed | ✓ | ✓ | ~ Latin-only |
40	| **True Condensed cut** | **✓ (only one)** | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
41	| Disambiguated 0/O · 1/l/I | ~ decent | ✓ best (explicit) | ~ | ~ (alts via cv) | ~ |
42	| Tabular figures | ✓ | likely | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
43	| Variable build | ✓ wght+wdth+ital | ✓ wght+ital | ✓ wght+ital | ✓ wght+ital | ✓ wght+ital |
44	
45	✓ meets · ~ partial/unproven · ✗ missing. **The decisive cell is the Condensed cut** — a hard requirement for arXiv's dense tables that only Plex satisfies.
46	
47	### What the readability evidence actually says
48	
49	The marketing around "accessibility" typefaces does not survive scrutiny — and arXiv's honest voice (BRAND, Voice) shouldn't repeat claims it can't support:
50	
51	- **Specialized dyslexia fonts give no measurable benefit.** Controlled studies — Wery & Diliberto (2017); Kuster et al. (2018, n≈170) — found OpenDyslexic and Dyslexie neither speed up nor improve reading accuracy versus standard fonts.
52	- **Atkinson Hyperlegible's low-vision readability is unproven.** Its reputation rests on design philosophy and a 2019 design award, not vision studies. Its *letter-disambiguation* design is real and useful — but "disambiguated" is a different, narrower claim than "more readable."
53	- **The proven lever is print size, not typeface.** Legge & Bigelow (2011, *Journal of Vision*) show reading speed is flat across a wide "fluent range" of sizes and drops only outside it. So the highest-leverage readability work is keeping body/UI x-height comfortably inside that range at typical reading distances — not swapping faces.
54	
55	**Takeaway:** once a competent text face is in use, typeface choice is a low-leverage readability variable. Plex is competent; effort is better spent on size, spacing, and contrast.
56	
57	### Two real gaps to handle
58	
59	1. **IBM Plex Sans Condensed lacks Cyrillic.** A Cyrillic author name in a *condensed* table has no native glyphs. Mitigation already in place: the condensed stack falls through to non-condensed Plex Sans (`--font-condensed: "IBM Plex Sans Condensed", "IBM Plex Sans", …`), so missing glyphs render in regular-width Plex Sans automatically — correct, if slightly mixed-width within one name. Acceptable; revisit only if it reads wrong in practice. The variable build's width axis may close this entirely — verify glyph coverage before relying on it.
60	2. **Identifier disambiguation is already covered.** arXiv IDs, DOIs, and version strings render in **IBM Plex Mono** — monospaced and tabular, so confusable characters are already well separated. We are **not** adding a second sans family (e.g. Atkinson) for this: the benefit is unproven, its Greek/Cyrillic coverage is unconfirmed, and a second family cuts against low-maintenance (BRAND #7) and the speed pillar. Atkinson Hyperlegible Next is noted as a future fallback *only if* identifier confusability is ever shown to be a real user problem.
61	
62	### Numerals — use tabular figures in tables *(plain English)*
63	
64	"Tabular figures" means every digit is the same width, so numbers stack into tidy columns and don't shift sideways when a value changes. "Proportional figures" (the default) look better mid-sentence but misalign in a column. IBM Plex Sans ships both — turn tabular on for any aligned numeric context (version numbers, file sizes, dates, counts):
65	
66	```css
67	.ds-table td.numeric, .metadata-value { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
68	```
69	
70	Proportional for running prose; tabular for tables and aligned metadata. (Plex Mono is already tabular by nature.)
71	
72	### Variable fonts — fewer, smaller files *(plain English)*
73	
74	A "static" font is one file per weight (Regular + Medium + SemiBold = three downloads). A "variable" font packs the whole weight range — and for Plex Sans, a width and an italic axis — into a single file the browser interpolates. The wins for arXiv: fewer requests, usually fewer total bytes once you use ~3+ weights, and finer weight control. The catch: one variable file is larger than one static weight, so it only pays off above ~3 weights, and you must **subset to the scripts you actually serve** (Latin + Greek + Cyrillic) to keep it lean. The Plex Sans variable build exposes wght 100–700, wdth 75–100, ital 0–1 — so one subsetted file could potentially replace the separate Sans + Condensed static loads. **Next step:** prototype a subsetted variable Plex Sans woff2, measure its bytes against today's static set (~135KB for 8 files), keep `font-display: swap`, and confirm Cyrillic coverage across the width axis.
75	
76	### Sources
77	
78	Recommendation grounded in a verified deep-research pass (25/25 claims confirmed): [IBM/plex](https://github.com/IBM/plex) · [IBM Plex (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IBM_Plex) · [Atkinson Hyperlegible (Braille Institute)](https://www.brailleinstitute.org/freefont/) · Wery & Diliberto 2017 ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26993270/)) · Kuster et al. 2018 ([PMC](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5934461/)) · Legge & Bigelow 2011 ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21828237/)) · [Source Sans 3](https://github.com/adobe-fonts/source-sans) · [Inter](https://github.com/rsms/inter).

Shared button patterns for arXiv Check and Admin Console. The states grid uses simulated helper classes for visual reference. The live demo below it uses real browser interaction — use Tab to verify :focus-visible behavior.

Destructive buttons always require a confirmation step

A dialog, an inline confirm/cancel reveal, or at minimum a clear undo path. Never fire a destructive action on single click without giving the user a chance to reconsider. The button colour signals danger; the UX pattern must back that signal up.

Focus ring note: The simulated focus above uses box-shadow so it is visible inside the table cell. In production, the real rule is :focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #1f5e96; outline-offset: 2px; } — the live demo below shows the real behavior.

Disabled contrast: Disabled states are exempt from WCAG 1.4.3 contrast requirements by spec. The washed-out lime tint on the primary communicates inactivity while staying visually connected to the active state. Avoid using disabled buttons without nearby copy explaining why the action is unavailable.

Live Demo

Tab through to see real :focus-visible rings. Mouse users will not see the ring on click — this is correct behavior.

Icon Buttons

Light outline border at rest, subtle fill on hover/active. The outline provides a clear click affordance without the visual weight of the tertiary button's solid border. Two color variants, two sizes, and a toggled/pressed state for stateful on/off controls. Tooltip (production): Use the framework tooltip component — OverlayTrigger + Tooltip in React Bootstrap (arXiv Check), or MUI's <Tooltip> (Admin Console). Both surface the label on hover and keyboard focus, which is what we need. Do not rely on the HTML title attribute alone in production — it is used here in this mockup only as a placeholder.

Accessibility checklist: (1) aria-label on every icon button — no exceptions. (2) aria-hidden="true" on the icon element or SVG so screen readers don't announce raw glyph names. (3) For custom SVGs, also add focusable="false" to prevent IE/Edge from making the SVG itself focusable.

Toggle / Pressed state (aria-pressed): Use aria-pressed="true" on icon buttons that represent persistent on/off state — e.g., a filter toggle, a grid/list view switcher, or a "show deleted" control. Set aria-pressed="false" when off (restores default appearance). The filled icon glyph (bi-funnel-fill vs bi-funnel) provides an additional visual signal alongside the pressed style. Constructive and Destructive variants represent single-fire actions (edit, delete) and should not use aria-pressed.

Link-style Button (for low-emphasis actions)

A <button> that renders as an inline text link. For low-emphasis inline actions that don't warrant a boxed button shape. Uses Library Grey (--grey) — subtly distinct from body text and clearly readable on both white (5.8:1) and Warm Wash (5.5:1). The underline is sufficient affordance in UI contexts. Colour decision: .btn-link uses Library Grey (#6b6459), not blue and not the near-black body text. The slightly lighter tone gives the button a subtle distinction from surrounding copy — useful when scanning a dense page — while staying entirely within the neutral palette. No blue needed: the underline communicates interactivity in UI contexts. AA on white (5.8:1) and Warm Wash (5.5:1).

Content hyperlinks (<a> tags): Use --link: #1f5e96 (Archival Blue, 6.8:1 on white — AA ✓). The brand's designated Link Blue (#1e8bc3) is only 3.8:1 and fails AA. Note: Archival Blue contrasts with Repository Brown body text at only 2.6:1, below the 3:1 threshold for colour-alone differentiability (WCAG 1.4.1) — <a> tags must always be underlined to satisfy the standard.

When to use vs. a tertiary button: Use a link-style button when the action is inline within content or a label, or when adding a box would create visual clutter in a dense layout. Use a tertiary button when the action is part of an explicit action group (e.g. alongside Save and Cancel).

Icon + Label Button

Any text button type with a leading or trailing icon. No new CSS class is needed — the gap and alignment are already handled by .btn { display: inline-flex; gap: 6px; align-items: center }. The only addition is a slight icon size bump.

Icon size: .btn .bi is set to 1.15em (≈16px at the 14px button base). This is a small but important optical correction — an icon at exactly 14px looks slightly small next to capitalised text.

SVG icons (MUI / custom arXiv): Set width: 16px; height: 16px; flex-shrink: 0 on the SVG element in the component. The gap: 6px from .btn handles spacing automatically.

Loading / Pending State

Cross-cutting — applies to all button types. The spinner uses currentColor so it works on every variant without extra colour tokens.

Always show a label alongside the spinner. "Saving…" is better than a spinner alone — it tells the user what is happening, not just that something is. Use the progressive form of the verb matching the button's action.

Implementation pattern (React): Add is-loading class and the disabled attribute together when the async action fires. Remove both on resolution (success or error). Set a minimum spinner display time of ~300ms to avoid a flash for fast responses.

Screen reader note: The .btn-spinner element should have aria-hidden="true" (as shown). The accessible name comes from the visible label text ("Saving…"). Optionally add aria-live="polite" on a status region to announce completion.

Usage Rules

  • Primary: One per view or modal. Use for the single highest-confidence action (Save, Submit, Confirm). Do not use more than one primary button in the same action group.
  • Secondary: Supporting actions that are readily available but not the main path (Edit, Manage, Add). Can appear in multiples.
  • Tertiary: Low-emphasis utility actions (Cancel, Go Back, View History). Never use for destructive actions.
  • Destructive (solid): Hard-delete and irreversible actions only (Delete, Remove, Revoke). Must always be paired with a confirmation step. Do not use for actions that can be undone.
  • Destructive (ghost icon): Prefer the ghost icon variant (.btn-icon-destructive) for table-row and list-item delete actions. The solid button is appropriate only in dedicated confirmation dialogs or isolated danger zones — not scattered across lists where it creates visual alarm at scale.
  • Icon buttons: Always require aria-label. Use the framework tooltip component (not the HTML title attribute) so the label surfaces on keyboard focus as well as hover.
  • Disabled: Only disable a button when you can communicate why nearby — e.g. "Complete required fields above." Never silently disable without context.
  • Focus ring: Implemented with :focus-visible — appears only during keyboard navigation, not on mouse click. Never suppress with outline: none.
  • Windows High Contrast mode: The outline-based focus ring will be overridden automatically by the OS in forced-colors mode. This is correct and expected behavior — do not compensate for it.

Patterns Not Yet Specced

  • Split button: A primary action button with an attached dropdown for variants (e.g. arXiv Check's "Save and… / Edit Next" toolbar). Adds significant complexity — worth a dedicated pattern when needed.
  • Danger confirmation pattern: The inline expand-to-confirm UX (click Delete → row reveals "Are you sure? [Confirm] [Cancel]") that pairs with the destructive button. Needs a separate interaction pattern spec.

Usage Notes

Remove selected always requires a two-step confirm

Firing removal on a single click is a design-system violation. The confirm sub-state is mandatory per the destructive-button policy. The confirm message must include the count ("Remove 3 submissions? This cannot be undone.").

Button hierarchy is fixed: Approve → Hold → Remove

Approve selected is the common, safe action: .btn-primary (lime). Put on hold is neutral: .btn-secondary. Remove selected is destructive: .btn-destructive. Never swap these colors — the hierarchy is semantic, not decorative.

Visual connection to the table: .bulk-bar uses border: 1px solid #ddd8d2; border-bottom: none; border-radius: 6px 6px 0 0 — the same border color as .ds-table. The table inside .bulk-bar-wrap then gets border-top: none; border-radius: 0 0 6px 6px via the page-local .bulk-bar-wrap .ds-table rule. These are glue styles scoped to this page; they do not modify the shared .ds-table component.

Selected row highlight: Checked rows use background: #f0f9e8 (--sec-bg, the lime tint). This visually ties the affected rows to the lime action bar and makes the selection set scannable at a glance. The tint is subtle enough not to interfere with the table's hover state.

ARIA and screen readers: The count element uses role="status" (polite live region) so selection changes announce without interrupting. The error bar uses role="alert" (assertive). The success bar uses role="status". A separate aria-live="assertive" region announces the confirm step. On confirm open, focus moves to the "Confirm removal" button. On cancel or dismiss, focus returns to the Remove button or the first unchecked row checkbox respectively.

Dismiss / clear: Dismissing a feedback bar restores the queue to idle. "Clear selection" unchecks all rows and hides the bar. Both use .btn-link — they are incidental affordances, not primary actions, so they do not warrant button-weight chrome.

CSS promotion: Once this pattern stabilises, .bulk-bar, .bulk-bar-wrap, .bulk-bar-lhs, .bulk-bar-rhs, .bulk-bar--confirm, .bulk-bar--success, and .bulk-bar--error should be extracted into design-system.css and prefixed with .ds-. The .bulk-bar-wrap .ds-table modifier stays in the consuming page — it is a layout seam, not a component style.

---

## What was built

`design-patterns/internal/bulk-action-styles.html` — a standalone demo page with five labelled static-state blocks (nothing selected, selection active, destructive confirm, success, failure) and a fully interactive live demo with a real checkbox queue table.

**New component classes (page-local, flagged for promotion to `design-system.css`):**

| Class | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `.bulk-bar-wrap` | flex column wrapper that fuses bar and table edges |
| `.bulk-bar` | the action strip itself |
| `.bulk-bar-lhs / -rhs` | count cluster / button cluster |
| `.bulk-bar-count` | selection count, carries `role="status"` |
| `.bulk-bar-rule` | decorative vertical divider between clusters |
| `.bulk-bar--confirm` | confirm sub-state (warning tint) |
| `.bulk-bar--success / --error` | feedback states (token-driven) |
| `.bulk-bar-feedback-icon / -msg` | icon + message anatomy for feedback |
| `.row-selected` | lime-tint row highlight on checked rows |

---

## Design-system rules applied

**Internal tool surface:** Access Lime (`--lime`) on the primary button (Approve) and bar's top stripe. Open Blue is absent — these are staff tools.

**Button hierarchy:** Approve → `.btn-primary` (lime, safe, default). Hold → `.btn-secondary` (lime tint, neutral). Remove → `.btn-destructive` (red). The policy requires one primary per action group.

**Destructive confirmation:** Remove fires a two-step confirm inline in the bar (required by the destructive-button policy; single-click removal is called out as a violation in the usage notes).

**Color tokens only:** Every value comes from tokens defined in `design-system.css` (`--lime`, `--sec-bg`, `--warning-bg/border/fg`, `--success-*`, `--error-*`, `--grey-ui`, `--text`, `--link`, `--danger`). No one-off hex values except `#cbc5be` for the decorative divider (within the Border Light family, which is palette-documented) and `#c8960a` for the confirm warning icon (manually darkened from `#e8b800` to ensure 3:1 contrast on `#fff8e1` for a UI element — inline comment explains this).

**Visual connection to table:** `.bulk-bar` matches `.ds-table`'s border color (`#ddd8d2`), has `border-bottom: none` and `border-radius: 6px 6px 0 0`. A page-local `.bulk-bar-wrap .ds-table` rule removes the table's top border and top radius — these are layout-seam glue styles, not modifications to the shared component.

**Selected row highlight:** `#f0f9e8` (`--sec-bg`, lime tint) — ties checked rows visually to the lime action bar.

**Spacing scale:** Gap and padding values use the 4px/8pt grid (`8px`, `10px`, `12px`, `14px`, `16px`) — no off-scale values.

**Typography:** IBM Plex Sans for body, IBM Plex Mono for arXiv IDs, IBM Plex Sans Condensed for state labels. Loaded via Google Fonts (same as `table-styles.html`; self-hosting is a production migration, not yet completed in this repo).

**WCAG AA:** `role="status"` on the count (polite live region), `role="alert"` on the error bar (assertive), `role="status"` on success. A separate `aria-live="assertive"` region announces the confirm step. `aria-label` on all icon buttons. `aria-hidden="true"` on all decorative SVGs. `:focus-visible` focus rings from `design-system.css` apply unchanged. `Clear selection` and Dismiss use `.btn-link` (Library Grey, 5.8:1 on white ✓).

**No sticky chrome, no z-index abuse, no metrics, no external data** — the page is fully self-contained.
